papers.title: Algebraic decomposition and topological fibrations of the $U(4) \to SU(2)$ quotient space
papers.abstract: We investigate the algebraic and topological properties of the unitary group $U(4)$ subjected to a non-standard continuous symmetry breaking cascade down to an $SU(2)_H$ subgroup. By explicitly embedding the unbroken $SU(2)_H$ symmetry into the lower-right quadrant of the fundamental matrix representation, we demonstrate that the resulting 12-dimensional quotient space, $SU(4)/SU(2)_H$, undergoes a strictly asymmetric geometric partition. This specific breaking pattern uniquely isolates an 8-dimensional sector that retains closed commutation relations, forming a rigorous $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ Lie subalgebra. Concurrently, it isolates a 4-dimensional off-diagonal sector that fails to close algebraically, generating a purely non-linear topological coset. By analyzing the global spherical fibrations of the manifold, we show that this non-linear territory reduces to a $\mathbb{C}P^1 \cong S^2$ base space. Consequently, continuous mappings from a 3-dimensional spatial boundary are classified by the third homotopy group, $\pi_3(S^2) \cong \mathbb{Z}$, guaranteeing absolute vacuum stability via the integer-quantized Hopf invariant. Ultimately, this framework demonstrates that a non-simple unitary group can organically provide a mathematically rigorous geometric template capable of simultaneously accommodating both continuous gauge symmetries and stable, non-perturbative topological sectors.

papers.title: Foundations of Wilson lines and loops from basic concepts to gauge field reconstruction
papers.abstract: This review presents a concise and unified treatment of Wilson lines and Wilson loops in continuum gauge theory, emphasizing their interpretation as parallel transport and their status as gauge covariant transporters and gauge invariant loop observables. Starting from the problem of comparing charged fields at separated points, we derive the path ordered exponential formulation and collect the key kinematical identities: gauge covariance, composition under path concatenation, inversion, and base point dependence. We then explain how local information is encoded in suitable small segment and small loop limits, and how these limits enter reconstruction questions for the underlying gauge connection. Seen as an inverse problem, this perspective clarifies how much of the gauge connection is encoded in loop observables and why traced Wilson loops, while gauge invariant, are intrinsically lossy without additional input. Special attention is given to clarifying common sources of confusion, in particular the distinction between untraced holonomies and traced Wilson loops, and the role of reference path choices when relating open transports to based loop data. The presentation is intended to serve both as an entry point for newcomers and as a compact reference for readers in high energy theory, mathematical physics, and related fields.

papers.title: Horizon-Boundary Localization of the Hawking Temperature in a Weak AdS/CFT Extension
papers.abstract: We establish a conditional boundary-localization statement for the Hawking temperature. For a static, Euclideanizable black hole with a non-degenerate horizon, the temperature is determined entirely by the first non-vanishing near-horizon data. This result is obtained consistently through three approaches: removal of the Euclidean conical defect, the horizon boundary term in the two-dimensional Gauss-Bonnet theorem, and a complex residue calculation. In asymptotically anti-de Sitter spacetime, the Euclidean time periodicity selected at the horizon extends to the conformal boundary, so the boundary conformal field theory inherits the same thermal period up to time normalization. This provides only a weak, temperature-sector extension of the AdS/CFT framework and does not imply a full duality. For dynamical spherical spacetimes, the Hamilton-Jacobi analysis selects the trapping or apparent horizon as the local thermal boundary, whereas a separated event horizon is generally not associated with the relevant pole. Vaidya and charged-Vaidya examples support this boundary-selection picture and reduce to the standard stationary result when the horizons coincide. The construction is further checked using anti-de Sitter black holes, numerical contour calculations, limiting cases, and an extremal counterexample. The result concerns where the Hawking temperature is localized and does not replace the quantum-field-theoretic mechanism of Hawking radiation.

papers.title: Finite quantum gravity in locally conformally flat spacetime through covariant spectral regularization
papers.abstract: Pure gravity quantum gravity (pure gravity QG) is non-renormalizable at two and higher loop level. One of the main characteristics of objects occurring in QG is their Lorentz covariance. QG necessitates the analysis of a collection of Lorentz covariant terms of higher and higher order, which is not feasible using renormailization. This paper describes how the regularization technique known as covariant spectral regularization (CSR) can be used to analyze Lorentz covariant 4-tensor valued measures on Minkowski space. The graviton vacuum polarization tensor is cast as such a measure and CSR is used to obtain a well defined and finite function representing this tensor. This is then used to compute the Feynman amplitudes for examples of one-loop, two-loop and $n$-loop graviton-graviton scattering in pure gravity QG. The CSR method results in functions (densities) representing divergent Feynman integrals without requiring renormalization or counterterms. Therefore it can be used to analyze arbitrarily complicated multiloop QG Feynman diagrams without being crippled by a proliferation of counterterms, as is classical QG.

papers.title: Probing generalized equation of state for dark energy with latest cosmological probes
papers.abstract: Baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements from DESI DR2 have strengthened indications of a time-evolving dark energy. In this paper, we investigate observational constraints on the generalized equation of state (GEoS) for dark energy, $w(a) = w_0 - w_\beta (a^{\beta}- 1)/\beta$, with latest data from UV and X-ray observations of high-redshift quasars, DESI DR2 BAO, Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data (including lensing) from Planck and the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT), and Pantheon+ Type Ia Supernovae (SNe Ia). The full Quasar+BAO+CMB+SNe Ia data combination yields stringent constraints on the EoS parameters of $w_0=-0.840^{+0.057}_{-0.084}$, $w_\beta=-0.90^{+0.88}_{-0.23}$, and $\beta=2.2^{+2.4}_{-5.2}$. Specially, the $\beta$ parameter, which describe a broad range of dark energy evolution, is in perfect agreement with the Chevallier--Polarski--Linder model ($\beta=1$) -- the most widely used two-parameter parametrizations of dynamical dark energy. We also compare GEoS with other dynamical dark-energy parametrizations including CPL, Barboza--Alcaniz (BA) and Jassal--Bagla--Padmanabhan (JBP), and report three key findings. Firstly, we find compelling evidence for dynamical dark energy: all four EoS parametrizations yield lower information criterion (IC) values than $\Lambda$CDM for the full data combination, indicating a preference for EoS parametrizations under the Akaike information criterion (AIC) and the variance-based deviance information criterion (DIC). Secondly, although the unified phenomenological framework GEoS performs better than JBP, the current data do not strongly discriminate among different EoS parametrizations. Thirdly, the EoS trajectories of GEoS, CPL, and BA exhibit qualitatively similar transitions from the phantom regime at higher redshifts to the quintessence regime at late times, while the JBP parametrization exhibits a nonmonotonic evolution.

papers.title: Two Cosmological Histories in a New Exponential Infrared $f(T)$ Teleparallel Gravity: Implications for the Hubble Tension and the Low-$\ell$ Planck TT--EE Tension
papers.abstract: We investigate a particular case of the New Exponential Infrared $f(T)$ teleparallel gravity model with the same number of free parameters as the standard $\Lambda$CDM model. Remarkably, due to the two real branches of the Lambert function $W$, the model admits two distinct cosmological solutions, denoted by $f^{(I)}$CDM and $f^{(II)}$CDM. The former exhibits a late-time phantom crossing, whereas the latter predicts an effective dark-energy density evolving from negative to positive values. Using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis of the Planck CMB, DESI BAO, and Type Ia supernova data, we find that the $f^{(II)}$CDM branch develops a bimodal posterior distribution in the primordial parameters $A_s$ and $\tau_{ reio}$ for the Planck-only dataset. We show that this bimodality originates from the tension between the low-$\ell$ TT and EE likelihoods, which becomes pronounced in models exhibiting a significantly enhanced late ISW contribution relative to the $\Lambda$CDM model. Moreover, the inclusion of background observations drives this branch toward cosmologically unacceptable parameter values, rendering it observationally unviable. The $f^{(I)}$CDM branch, on the other hand, remains observationally viable, yielding $H_0=73.43\pm0.69~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ for the Planck-only dataset and $H_0=72.55\pm0.32~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ after including DESI, substantially alleviating the Hubble tension. Although this branch provides a slightly better fit than $\Lambda$CDM for Planck-only data, the addition of background observations reverses this preference in favor of the standard $\Lambda$CDM model. These results show that the cosmological viability of this model critically depends on the choice of the Lambert $W$ branch, with only the $f^{(I)}$CDM solution remaining compatible with current cosmological observations.

papers.title: $f(Q,T)$ Gravity with Barrow Holographic Dark Energy and Massive Neutrinos: DESI DR2 Constraints and Implications for the Hubble Tension
papers.abstract:
We study a modification of symmetric teleparallel gravity in which the function $f(Q,T)$ is linear in the non-metricity scalar $Q$ and the trace $T$ of the energy-momentum tensor, combined with a Barrow holographic dark energy (BHDE) density built from the Granda-Oliveros infrared cutoff. The resulting background equations are solved in a modified version of 	exttt{hi\_class} and constrained with Pantheon+ supernovae, 32 cosmic chronometer $H(z)$ points, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, and Planck 2018 CMB distance priors, sampled with MontePython. Two versions of the model are considered, one with the neutrino sector held massless and one with the sum of neutrino masses $\Sigma m_
u$ left free. Across five data combinations, $H_0$ falls between 67.5 and 72.3 km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, closer to the Planck value when cosmic chronometers dominate the fit and closer to the SH0ES value when Pantheon+ is included; adding $\Sigma m_
u$ as a free parameter raises $H_0$ in four of the five combinations, by amounts ranging from a few hundredths of a km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ up to about 1.5 km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, while the CMB-only combination shifts slightly the other way, and the fit uncertainties loosen throughout. The 95\% upper bound on $\Sigma m_
u$ ranges from 0.13 to 0.22 eV depending on the data combination, comparable to standard $\Lambda$CDM constraints. Comparison with $\Lambda$CDM through the Akaike and Bayesian Information Criteria gives mixed results: the extended model is favored once Pantheon+ is included, particularly with massive neutrinos, but is disfavored for CMB-only and CMB+BAO fits, where the improvement in $\chi^2$ does not offset the larger parameter count. The Barrow exponent $\Delta$ stays below 0.005 throughout, and the Granda-Oliveros parameters $\lambda$ and $\gamma$ remain near 1 and 0.5 across all combinations.

papers.title: Variational Principles for Hierarchical Systems of Equations
papers.abstract: A unified construction of variational principles (VP) is applied to hierarchical systems of equations. The adjoint set of equations involved in this construction differ from the original hierarchy set in important ways. Notably, upward and downward nature of hierarchy are reversed between the two sets, as are boundary conditions and, most significantly, whether or not the equations are factorizable. These features may make for ease of solving one of the two sets and thereby for usefulness of the VP themselves that employ both.

papers.title: From Poincare Invariance to Gauge Theories: Yang-Mills and General Relativity
papers.abstract: This article is founded on two fundamental principles: the principle field equations introduced in Refs. \cite{S, S1, S2} and the Fock-Ivanenko covariant derivatives \cite{FI, F}. The former yields the equations of motion for free fields of arbitrary spin and helicity. In the massless case, it also dictates that Lorentz transformations for tensor fields acquire an additional term, which takes the form of a gauge transformation \cite{W, S1}. The latter principle, the Fock-Ivanenko derivative, introduces interactions based on the intrinsic and Poincare groups. This framework allows us to recover a complete Yang-Mills theory, as well as general relativity in the connection-based formulations of Palatini and Ashtekar, both of which are theories with local gauge symmetries. While the standard approach begins with the symmetries of a matter action, we will instead derive dynamics directly from Poincare invariance. This perspective reveals that for free fields, Lorentz invariance induces the gauge symmetry of massless tensors. A proper definition of these gauge transformations, in turn, requires the covariant derivatives provided by the Fock-Ivanenko approach. Considering matter fields, we derive the interacting Dirac equation in the presence of Yang-Mills and gravitational fields from its free counterpart.

papers.title: Klein-Gordon and Dirac Oscillators in a Constant-Curvature Fock-Lorentz Background
papers.abstract: We propose a controlled momentum-space dual of the Fock--Lorentz (FL) transformations and use it to derive a deformed relativistic mass shell. Restricting the FL conformal factor to the cosmological-frame world line $\vx=0$, the invariant relation takes the form $(E^{2}-\vp^{2}c^{2})(1+ct/R)^{2}=m_{0}^{2}c^{4}$, which is equivalent to the standard special-relativistic dispersion law with a time-dependent apparent mass $\mapp(t)=m_{0}/(1+ct/R)$. Canonical quantization then yields Klein--Gordon (KG) and Dirac equations containing a slowly varying mass scale. We show explicitly that squaring the Dirac equation reproduces the KG operator, modulo first-order corrections proportional to $\dot\mapp$ that are suppressed by the ratio of the Compton wavelength to the FL scale. The construction is not presented as a unique covariant phase-space theory; rather, it is a world-line ansatz designed to isolate the spectral consequences of the FL conformal factor. As applications, we study the one-dimensional KG and Dirac oscillators. In the adiabatic regime, governed by the small parameter $\epsilon=c/(R\omega)\ll1$, closed-form instantaneous spectra are obtained. The Dirac-oscillator calculation is carried out in component form and then reduced to the physical spinor spectrum, thereby avoiding the double counting of the upper and lower component ladders. Dimensionless plots illustrate the apparent-mass drift, the induced spectral evolution, and the domain of adiabatic validity. For cosmological values of $R$, non-adiabatic corrections are entirely negligible; in the formal limit $t\to\infty$ the apparent mass tends to zero and, for fixed quantum number, the instantaneous levels collapse toward $E=0$.

papers.title: Odd-Parity Perturbations of Geometrically Regular Black Holes with Hedgehog Scalar Hair
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study linear perturbations of a geometrically regular black hole supported by a constrained $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ scalar triplet in the hedgehog configuration. Since the individual background scalars depend explicitly on the angular coordinates, the decoupling of polar and axial perturbations cannot be concluded from the spherical form of the metric or the energy--momentum tensor alone. To settle this point, we introduce the polar and axial metric and triplet amplitudes simultaneously and derive the corresponding projections of the radiative linearized Einstein--matter equations for $\ell\geq2$. The polar equations contain only polar amplitudes, whereas the axial equations contain only axial amplitudes; hence, the two off-diagonal blocks vanish at linear order. The resulting odd-parity sector forms a closed Einstein--scalar system in which a tangent perturbation of the scalar triplet is coupled to the Regge--Wheeler metric amplitudes. We show that its scalar equation has a second-order hyperbolic principal part whenever $K_Y\neq0$, and that, for the nonlinear kinetic function supporting the background, $K_Y>0$ throughout the black-hole exterior. The coefficient of the direct metric--scalar mixing is largest at the event horizon and decreases as $r^{-4}$ at large distance, while the metric block in the vacuum limit reproduces the standard Regge--Wheeler equation and potential; the scalar kinetic coefficient simultaneously vanishes, so the full operator changes rank. These results establish linear parity decoupling and the consistency of the closed axial equations. They do not, however, constitute a proof of mode stability, which requires the reduction of the complete quadratic action.
